title: Light Tuna in Water, Drained Solids

content.title: About
content.content: Light tuna in water, drained solids is a canned tuna product that has been pressed to remove excess liquid. It is ready to eat, has a mild flavor and tender texture, and works well in salads, sandwiches, and quick meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tuna belongs to the mackerel family and is one of the richest sources of omega‑3 fatty acids.
Canning in its own water preserves more nutrients compared with oil‑packed versions.
Light tuna is usually taken from younger fish, resulting in lighter‑colored, softer meat.
In Japan tuna is often used for sushi and sashimi, while the canned version is popular in Europe and the US.
Tuna can be caught using traditional methods or modern selective nets that reduce by‑catch.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3
items.content: Omega‑3 fatty acids support heart health, help lower triglyceride levels, and reduce inflammation.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Tuna provides complete protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: Light tuna contains less fat than oil‑packed varieties, making it suitable for lower‑calorie diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It is a good source of vitamin B12, niacin, and vitamin B6, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Tuna supplies selenium, phosphorus, and potassium, nutrients important for immunity and bone health.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to fish, including tuna.

items.title: Mercury content
items.content: Tuna can contain trace amounts of mercury; moderate consumption is advised, especially for children and pregnant women.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Canned tuna often contains added salt; people monitoring sodium intake should take this into account.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add tuna to salads, pasta, rice dishes, spread on bread, or use as a filling for wraps. The product is typically ready to eat and does not require further cooking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place. After opening, transfer to an airtight container and keep refrigerated, using within 2‑3 days.
